items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the multiple residence law and the multiple dwelling law, in
relation to requiring owners and agents of multiple residences and multiple
dwellings to provide names and contact information of residents to emergency
personnel
items.lawCode: Add §16, Mult Res L; add §15, Mult Dwell L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2294

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the multiple residence law and the multiple dwelling
law, in relation to requiring owners and agents of multiple residences
and multiple dwellings to provide names and contact information of resi-
dents to emergency personnel

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to ensure that emergency services are able
to determine the safety of the residents of a building after a fire.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the multiple residence law by adding a new section 16,
which provides for owners or agents of multiple residences to provide
emergency personnel names and contact information of affected residents
in the case of an emergency.

Section 2 amends the multiple dwelling law by adding a new section 15,
which provides for owners or agents of multiple dwelling to provide
emergency personnel names and contact information of affected residents
in the case of an emergency.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

On August 11, 2019, a fire in a Yonkers Apartment building displaced
eighty-six people displaced from their homes. The fire caused excessive
damage to the five-story building and took 60 firefighters.  Luckily, no
one was injured by the fire but during the blaze emergency responders
were unable to determine who was safely out of the building. When emer-
gency personnel contacted the building ownership to determine if every-
one was safely evacuated, it was difficult to get a list of who was
living in the building and their contact.

In the case of an emergency, first responders are best equipped to do
their job and prevent the loss of life when they are fully informed.
When triaging an emergency preventing the loss of life or injury is
critical but when the information required to do so is withheld this
task in even more difficult.

This bill seeks to help preserve the life and health of residents of
multiple dwelling/residence building by enabling emergency personnel to
have access to the information they need.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021/22: S240B (Mayer) / A10286 (Dinowitz): referred to Housing,
Construction and Community Development; advanced to third reading;
passed Senate

2019/20: S6918 (Mayer) referred to Rules (2019); referred to Housing,
Construction, and Community Development (2020)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2294A

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the multiple residence law and the multiple dwelling
law, in relation to requiring owners and agents of multiple residences
and multiple dwellings to provide names and contact information of resi-
dents to emergency personnel

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to ensure that emergency services are able
to ascertain the safety of the residents of a building in case of a fire
or other emergency.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the multiple residence law by adding a new section 16,
which directs owners or agents of multiple residences to provide emer-
gency personnel with the names and contact information of affected resi-
dents in the case of an emergency. Such names and contact information
shall not be disseminated, used or accessed for any other purposes.

Section 2 amends the multiple dwelling law by adding a new section 15,
which directs owners or agents of multiple dwellings to provide emergen-
cy personnel with the names and contact information of affected resi-
dents in the case of an emergency. Such names and contact information
shall not be disseminated, used or accessed for any other purposes.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

On August 11, 2019, a fire in a Yonkers apartment building displaced
eighty-six people from their homes. The fire caused excessive damage to
the five-story building. Sixty firefighters responded to the fire.
Fortunately, no one was injured but during the blaze emergency respon-
ders were unable to determine who was safely out of the building and who
might still be at risk. When emergency personnel contacted the building
owner to determine if everyone was safely evacuated, they had difficulty
obtaining a list with resident names and contact information.

In the case of an emergency, first responders are best equipped to
prevent the loss of life or injury when they are fully informed.

This bill seeks to preserve the life and health of residents of multiple
dwellings and multiple residences by providing emergency personnel with
the critical information they need to save lives during emergencies.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021/22: S240B (Mayer) / A10286 (Dinowitz): referred to Housing,
Construction and Community Development; advanced to third reading;
passed Senate

2019/20: S6918 (Mayer) referred to Rules (2019); referred to Housing,
Construction, and Community Development (2020)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires owners and agents of multiple residences and multiple dwellings to provide names and contact information of residents to emergency personnel upon the request of such personnel, where the physical safety of such residents must be accounted for by ascertaining their whereabouts.
